headings.text: 2. Wire the service into a deploy phase

blocks.html:
This page is about adding a new service, or wiring an existing one, into the Deploy App platform. It assumes you've read Architecture and the Development Guide.

What "integrating a service" means here

A product is integrated when:

  1. It runs as a workload in the cluster with its own namespace and overlay.
  2. It's registered with miniwerk via MW_PRODUCTS, so the RM UI knows it exists and presents it during onboarding.
  3. It trusts the in-cluster CA (issued by opendefense-cfssl), so it can talk to other platform services.
  4. It's reachable through Traefik at <product>.<OPENDEFENSE_HOST>, and at mtls.<product>.<OPENDEFENSE_HOST> too if it needs client-certificate auth.
  5. It's composed into the right phase under k8s/main/<env>/opendefense/.

battlelog, tak, and mtx are the three best worked examples. Copy from whichever is closest in shape to your service.

Step-by-step: adding a new service

1. Create the service folder

k8s/<service>/
├── base/
│   ├── kustomization.yaml
│   └── resources/
│       ├── namespace.yaml
│       ├── deployment.yaml
│       ├── service.yaml
│       └── ...                    # PVC, postgres, configmap, ...
└── overlays/
    ├── local/kustomization.yaml
    └── cloud/kustomization.yaml

If your service is a stateful web app with its own database, use k8s/battlelog/ as the template. Mirror its namespace: pattern (app-<service>) and its configMapGenerator shape so logs, metrics, and labels stay consistent.

2. Wire the service into a deploy phase

Add the overlay to both k8s/main/local/opendefense/kustomization.yaml and k8s/main/cloud/opendefense/kustomization.yaml:

resources:
  - ../../../opendefense-cfssl/overlays/local
  - ../../../opendefense-pki/overlays/local
  - ../../../opendefense-system/overlays/local
  - ../../../battlelog/overlays/local
  - ../../../<service>/overlays/local   # ← add

If your service depends on infrastructure that's missing from a phase, put the dependency in the correct earlier phase. Don't duplicate the dependency inside your service folder, and don't add a new service to k8s/pvarki-keycloak/. That aggregate is legacy and is documented as an anti-pattern in agents.md.

3. Register the product with miniwerk

The Rasenmaeher UI and API only know about a product once it appears in MW_PRODUCTS. Edit the literal in k8s/opendefense-system/base/kustomization.yaml:

configMapGenerator:
  - name: opendefense-miniwerk-env
    literals:
      - MW_DOMAIN=localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi
      - MW_PRODUCTS="kc,tak,mtx,<your-product-code>"

Use a short, lowercase product code (e.g. bl, tak, mtx). Whatever you pick is what the integration API uses to find your service. After the edit, re-run the miniwerk job: delete the existing one and let the manifest recreate it, or run task deploy if the configmap hash changes.

4. Plumb identity (Keycloak)

There are two patterns, depending on the service:

  • The service trusts platform-issued JWTs. It validates the Authorization: Bearer ... header against the Keycloak public key. No new realm config needed.
  • The service needs its own OIDC client. Add a Keycloak client definition to k8s/opendefense-system/keycloak-config/ and let the init job apply it through the realm import.

Look at how rmapi is wired today. It loads its JWT keys from a PVC populated by miniwerk and reads its OIDC config from a secret managed by external-secrets-operator.

5. Plumb certificates (CFSSL + trust-manager)

If your service initiates outbound mTLS calls, for example to other platform services, you need:

  1. A Certificate resource in your overlay pointing at the cluster issuer that fronts CFSSL. Look at k8s/opendefense-pki/ for the issuer name in each environment.
  2. A trust-manager Bundle distributing the CA bundle into your namespace. Reuse the bundle already produced in opendefense-pki. Don't create a new one. trust-manager runs in infra-phase2, so your service has to run in a later phase.

The _shared/rmapi-container-init component is a good reference for an init container that needs the CA in place before the main process starts.

6. Expose the service through Traefik

Add the routing in the overlay, not the base. Each overlay usually defines:

  • A standard IngressRoute for <product>.<OPENDEFENSE_HOST> (TLS via cert-manager).
  • An IngressRoute on the mtls entry point for mtls.<product>.<OPENDEFENSE_HOST>, with a TLSOption that requires a client certificate.

Locally, hostnames resolve through the loopback DNS record at localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi, so you don't need to touch /etc/hosts. On cloud, Zarf substitutes ###ZARF_VAR_OPENDEFENSE_HOST### at deploy time. Use the token in your overlay, never a hard-coded host.

If your service needs raw TCP (TAK, RTMPS, and so on), update both the Traefik entryPoints and the kind-config.yaml extra-port-mappings so the protocol reaches the cluster on the workstation.

7. Verify

# Render to catch syntax and missing references first
kubectl kustomize --enable-helm k8s/<service>/overlays/local

# Deploy
task deploy

# Watch the rollout
kubectl -n <namespace> get pods -w

# Confirm miniwerk re-ran and picked up the new MW_PRODUCTS value
kubectl -n opendefense-system logs job/opendefense-miniwerk

Then load the RM UI at https://localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi/ and check that the new product shows up in the onboarding flow.

API surface to integrate against

Your service code talks to the platform through two contracts:

  • Rasenmaeher API (rmapi). The REST API documented at the upstream Swagger (pvarki.github.io/python-rasenmaeher-api). Use it to query user and team context, and to register product-side resources during onboarding.
  • Keycloak. Standard OIDC. Tokens issued by the RASENMAEHER realm carry the user identity and group membership.

The compose upstream (pvarki/docker-rasenmaeher-integration) is still the most complete reference for the API contract while these docs fill in.

Conventions to keep

  • Namespace: app-<service> for application services, opendefense-<thing> for platform and infra services.
  • Resource names: prefix with the namespace stem (e.g. app-battlelog-..., opendefense-rmapi-...). Collisions across namespaces are easy to spot that way.
  • Labels and selectors: stable across base and overlay. Don't rename unless you mean to migrate.
  • Image references in base: use placeholder tags, then pin in the overlay.
  • One concern per PR. Adding the service folder is one PR, wiring routing is another, registering with miniwerk is a third. It keeps reviews quick.

Do not

  • Don't extend k8s/pvarki-keycloak/ with new services. Build a new service folder instead.
  • Don't invent a new CA. Use opendefense-cfssl plus trust-manager.
  • Don't bake OPENDEFENSE_HOST into base manifests. It's a deploy-time Zarf variable in cloud and a fixed hostname locally.
  • Don't stash credentials in ConfigMaps. Use external-secrets-operator with a Secret resource.
